observation.visible_scene: A person wearing a white short-sleeved shirt is on a glossy tiled floor (red-and-green mosaic pattern), in a push-up posture facing the camera, hands planted flat on the tiles. The scene is strongly backlit by sunlight streaming from a barred window behind, producing a bright lens flare that obscures the head and upper body. A door is at left, a metal bench/rack at right, and plants hang in the upper right. The camera and all background objects remain fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: From t=0.0 to roughly t=0.6-0.7 s, the torso and head descend toward the floor while the elbows bend: the body moves from a higher, more extended-arm plank position (frames 1-3) down to a low position with the head/chest near the tiles (frames 8-11).

From about t=0.7 s to the end (t=2.67 s), the body stays in the lowered position; the hands do not move and the chest/head remain close to the floor, i.e. a sustained bottom-of-push-up hold rather than a repeated up-down cycle.
During the hold, only small head/neck adjustments are visible (the head tilts and shifts side-to-side slightly between roughly frames 26-35), without a clear change in overall body height.
The feet/legs are never visible within the frame; only the upper body and arms are shown.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the descent seen at the start is the lowering phase of a single push-up rep already underway, or the end of a prior motion.
What happens after the clip ends (whether the person pushes back up or remains down) is not shown.
The exact hand spacing and full body alignment behind the torso are not visible.
uncertain_details: The face/head is hidden by the lens flare in the early frames, so head orientation is hard to read at the start.
The slight head movements during the hold could be a person adjusting gaze/neck or minor posture shifts; they do not indicate a new push-up rep.
It is unclear if the body height changes by a few millimeters in the final frames; the position is best described as a near-static low hold.
